CovariateSearcher — Function Reference

Source: FUNCTIONS.md

What this is: an agent-facing map of every function in R/, so future sessions don’t have to re-read the whole codebase. Originally generated from a full read of the pre-refactor code (v0.1.30). Last audited 2026-08-11 against v0.4.4: 29 files in R/, 142 top-level functions, 90 exports in NAMESPACE — every defined function appears below. Keep it in sync as the modular reorg lands.

Legend: Exp ✓ = exported (@export), · = internal/documented-internal. Side effects flag file writes, bbr:: calls, <<-, stop(), hardcoded paths. Nested = a closure defined inside another function (not top-level).

Housekeeping: this file is a dev/agent aid, not package content — ^FUNCTIONS\.md$ is in .Rbuildignore (done), so it doesn’t ship or trip R CMD check.

Cross-cutting hazards & consolidation candidates (read before any merge)

Duplicate implementations (merge targets — but preserve contracts): - .ext readers ×3: read_nonmem_ext (file-io.R → found/ofv/parameters, FINAL -1e9 line, flat+subdir), read_ext_file (monitoring-files.R → status/current_ofv/iterations/has_estimation_issues/…, last/current line, subdir-only), read_ext_iterations (plot_nonmem_iterations.R → tidy data.frame, consumed positionally by the sim sampler). Different OFV semantics + file locations — do not conflate. - .cov/.cor matrix parsers ×2: calculate_condition_number (model-output-tables.R, reconstructs lower-triangular) vs .read_nonmem_matrix (forest-plots.R, assumes labelled square). - $THETA name/trans parsers ×3: extract_params/extract_model_params (model-output-tables.R) vs inline in apply_covariate_model vs inline in create_covariate_table. - Categorical-level decode ×2+: decode_cov_level (model-output-tables.R, the only unit-tested fn) vs nested decode_level (forest-plots.R) vs the inline decode in model_add_cov. - Covariate formula algebra ×2 (highest risk): model_add_cov writes NONMEM factors; apply_covariate_model reconstructs the same math in R. Must stay in sync. Also, model_add_cov’s formula block is duplicated verbatim within itself (~L404-408 and ~L490-494). - name→tag idiom names(tags)[tags==name] repeated ~6× in scm-selective-forward.R + full_scm_search.R; overlaps get_covariate_tag_from_name. - “Get covariates” family (names lie about source): get_model_covariates_from_db (reads bbr files, returns tag values), get_model_covariates_from_files (reads bbr files, returns tag names), get_covariates_from_models (DB, many models). Do not collapse blindly. - Run-success test ×2 (added 2026-07-30 — must stay identical): get_model_status_from_files (file-io.R, returns a status string; used by base-model validation + discovery) and update_model_status_from_files’s nested read_all_model_files (validation.R, writes the DB row) now apply the same rule in the same order: run finished (.lst present, not incomplete) → usable OFV (non-NA, finite, abs <= 1e10, no parameter at abs >= 8.9999e5) → .cov present when require_cov_step. Both resolve output location via read_nonmem_lst()$file and look for the .cov in dirname() of it. Neither has a route to "completed" that skips the OFV test: a .lst reporting completion with a missing or unparseable .ext is failed in both. If they drift, a model’s verdict depends on which reader looked at it. completed_with_issues was retired from this path and is no longer produced anywhere in the package. The flag itself is threaded initialize_covariate_search(require_cov_step=) → validate_base_model_for_search + initialize_search_config (stored in search_config, before discover_existing_models runs) → read back via %||% TRUE by discovery, update_model_status_from_files and run_automated_scm_testing (which only overwrites it when the caller supplied it). Extended 2026-07-31: the agreement now also covers an unreadable listing — both readers call read_error failed (previously update_model_status_from_files reported it as in_progress, which the monitoring loop waits on forever), and both read listings only through .read_listing_lines() (latin1 + skipNul), never bare readLines(). The two readers still name the unfinished state differently — update_model_status_from_files writes "in_progress", get_model_status_from_files/discovery write "incomplete" — and both spellings sit in checkpoints already on disk, so neither can be renamed; any “is this still running?” guard must go through .is_pending_status() rather than an inline status vector.

Acceptance rule ×1 (consolidated 2026-08-07 — no longer a merge target): “does this model meet the criteria” (status completed + per-covariate-df ΔOFV threshold + RSE limit) used to be re-derived independently at every decision site. It now has one implementation, .evaluate_model_criteria() (scm-evaluation.R), read by select_best_model, .best_acceptable_model, get_significant_models_from_step/get_step_models, evaluate_removal_impacts, and create_scm_results_table’s nested get_selection_info; the RSE limit itself resolves only through .resolve_rse_threshold() (utilities.R). The phase argument is not cosmetic — forward and backward store delta_ofv with opposite signs and compare it in opposite directions, so a backward step judged with the forward default silently reports the wrong models. And a phase-aware evaluator is not by itself enough: the candidate pool handed to it must be phase-consistent too. A forward pick over a set that includes backward rows misreads every one of them — a removal that badly worsened the fit looks like a large improvement — no matter which phase was passed. This bites any search that begins with backward elimination, which then has such rows in the database from the start. .scm_backward_rows(db) (continue-search.R) is the row-level filter for this, and run_scm_selective_forward applies it at all four of its candidate pools; the test “every forward candidate pool in the file carries the phase filter” greps the source and fails if any pool lacks it, so a newly added fifth pool cannot silently reintroduce the misread. The filter tests phase OR action (via .is_removal_model), not phase alone: a retry of a backward removal is written phase="retry" yet later receives a backward-signed delta_ofv, so phase-only let it into every forward pool. Matching on action closes that because it is the same predicate validation.R:336 uses to choose the sign. The base row is matched by neither test (phase="base", action="base_model") and so stays in scope on purpose — the redemption-base fallback needs to find base_model_id in that same table. See the two-field note under R/continue-search.R for the sign-writer audit. One remaining exception, and it is deliberate: evaluate_removal_impacts calls the evaluator but discards its meets_threshold, recomputing meets_ofv & meets_rse without the status == "completed" term — by design, because eligibility there is the caller’s completed_models argument, and submit_and_wait_for_step() hands back that list wholesale under auto_submit = FALSE, so re-gating on DB status would stall the manual workflow. Do not “fix” it back to meets_threshold. (generate_scm_report was the other exception — no RSE term, df=1 hardcoded, final model by which.max(step_number). Rewritten 2026-08-07 to read every verdict from the evaluator and to track the final model through the accepted winners, so the report and the search can no longer disagree.) The companion invariant is the sign: .signed_delta_ofv() (utilities.R) is the one place the ΔOFV convention is chosen, off the same .is_removal_model() predicate, so a stored delta and the rule that reads it stay in agreement — see its direction note under R/utilities.R for when a caller may override it.

Schema declared in 5 places (must all stay in sync / all get stage): canonical initialize_search_database_core (19 cols as of 2026-07-30, created_by_search added) · self-heal required_cols in validation.R (13-col subset) · self-heal in scm-selective-forward.R · model-discovery.R rebuilds the 19-col row by hand · row-builders add_covariate_to_model/remove_covariate_from_model (bind_rows) + create_retry_model (order-sensitive rbind on a blanked db[1,] template — hence its .ensure_provenance_column() call). A checkpoint predating a new column is only migrated for created_by_search, via .ensure_provenance_column() in load_search_state/create_retry_model; the other four sites have no migration path.

action / phase vocabulary (display registry must cover all): - action written: base_model, add_covariate, remove_covariate, add_single_covariate, remove_single_covariate, retry, manual_modification. - phase written: base, forward_selection, covariate_removal, backward_elimination, retry, manual, individual_testing. - Display generators (generate_step_display/_changes_display/_step_description) only recognize {base_model, add_covariate, remove_covariate, retry} → everything else renders “Unknown: X”.

Confirmed bugs (fix during the relevant phase): - run_univariate_step error handler <- FIXED 2026-07-18: error handler used <- (handler-local) → thrown-error failures dropped from tracking → now <<- (scm-execution.R:153-154), matching the file’s existing <<- callbacks. - remove_covariate_from_model action label FIXED 2026-07-18 (A1): wrote action="remove_single_covariate" → “Unknown” in tables (backward path was only patched by scm-backward.R:155); now writes "remove_covariate" at root so manual removal displays correctly. - Retry misclassification FIXED 2026-07-18: grepl("\\d{3}$") flagged run100+ as retries → now grepl("^run\\d+001$") (was 6 sites; the 2 yaml-analysis helpers later removed in the dead-code sweep — remaining: process_estimation_issues, update_model_counter, generate_recovery_report, discover_models). Residual false positives only for normal models ending in 001 (run1001…). - Excluded-covariate “final testing” block in full_scm_search.R is dead (filters phase=="forward" which is never written; also gated by run_forward && !run_final_backward, false for full_scm). → retire (owner dropped excluded_only). - cat.power read-side bug FIXED 2026-07-19 (registry, Step ③): apply_covariate_model previously gated the categorical IF-parse branch on status=="cat" alone, so cat.power (e.g. dose 35/70/125/150) wrongly entered it (no IF(COV.EQ.x) block → mis-reconstructed). Now BOTH model_add_cov (write) and apply_covariate_model (read) dispatch on the registry’s categorical flag (get_covariate_formula(status, formula)$categorical): cat.linear → per-level IF/ELSEIF; everything else incl. cat.power → single factor from the same registry entry (nonmem write / r_eval read), so write & read can’t drift. - generate_phase removed 2026-07-18 (dead, unexported).

Rejected designs (considered, implemented, reverted — do not re-propose): - Gating model success on NONMEM’s termination verdict (tried and reverted 2026-08-07). The idea: have update_model_status_from_files consume read_nonmem_lst()$status == "failed" and mark the model failed, since the listing already classifies MINIMIZATION TERMINATED / FATAL ERROR and the caller was discarding it. It looks like free rigour. It is not: - It contradicts a deliberate decision stated at file-io.R:466-469 — “How minimisation ended is deliberately not part of it: a run that stopped on rounding errors but produced both is a success.” Success is a usable OFV plus a covariance matrix, nothing else. - MINIMIZATION TERMINATED DUE TO ROUNDING ERRORS matches hard_failure_patterns and is the most common non-SUCCESSFUL outcome in covariate work; such runs normally do produce a usable OFV and a .cov. Gating on it would have failed most usable covariate models, and the search would have reported “no significant covariates” — a wrong scientific answer, arrived at silently. - The gate returned before the .ext was read, so it also suppressed OFV/RSE recording for those rows: the OFV the run really did produce vanished from the database and from every report. - The obvious defence — make the hard-failure test order-aware, so a failure marker only counts when no success marker follows — has its own false negative. It asks “is there a success after the first failure”, so TERMINATED → SUCCESSFUL → TERMINATED reports completed. A three-$EST sequence (SAEM → IMP → FOCE) is ordinary, so this is not a corner case either. - The real convergence gate already exists and is require_cov_step: a successful covariance step is stronger evidence of identifiability than a termination string, and it is already threaded through init → config → both readers → .evaluate_model_criteria’s RSE rule. Net: read_nonmem_lst()$status stays a listing verdict that no caller treats as disqualifying, and both run-success readers keep the OFV+.cov test above.

Dependency/NAMESPACE hygiene — RESOLVED (verified 2026-07-28): mvtnorm, ggplot2, yspec are in Imports:; mrgsolve, devEMF in Suggests:. The 5 sim @exports that used to be missing (sample_individual_thetas, build_scenario_parameters, simulate_scenario_profiles, plot_exposure_forest+theme_forest, create_covariate_boxplots) are all in NAMESPACE now. Still un-declared: base-priority tools/grid/grDevices.

Package scaffolding

R/CovariateSearchr.R

Package-level scaffolding: _PACKAGE doc, the central @importFrom manifest, and the master globalVariables block. No functions.

Notes: No function definitions. Holds the central utils::globalVariables(...) block (~60 names: DB columns + dplyr-chain vars + per-function NSE vars for extract_params/get_param2/model_report/submit_and_wait_for_step) and the central @importFrom manifest on "_PACKAGE" (dplyr, tibble, bbr, yaml, readr, purrr, stringr, stats, utils, data.table, flextable, officer, tidyr, rlang). This block is the single most important thing to keep intact when moving NSE-heavy functions.

Validates the spec (equal vector lengths, STATUS ∈ con/cat, one Category per covariate across rows, covariate/id/time columns present) and the FORMULA vocab (built-ins — con: linear/power/exponential, cat: linear/power — else an expression that parses and references cov). REFERENCE comes from baseline only (Time == 0, first row per ID): round(median, 2) for con, most-prevalent level for cat. LEVELS comes from the FULL dataset, not baseline — unique non-NA values of the whole column, so a level that only appears away from baseline (e.g. a time-varying dose under a power formula) is still captured; ordered to match yaml_data[[cov]]$values (falls back to lexicographic sort() only when the yaml lists no values), NA for con. Cross-checks those levels against the yaml, and derives TIME_DEPENDENT from the full data (>1 distinct value within a subject); optional INIT column data, aligned spec vectors, yaml_data (needs $<cov>$values per categorical covariate — supplies both the legal set and the level ordering) data.frame in spec-row order, columns PARAMETER, COVARIATE, STATUS, FORMULA, LEVELS, REFERENCE, TIME_DEPENDENT[, INIT] stop() on spec/vocab errors, on a categorical covariate absent from yaml_data, and on a data level not defined in yaml_data; warning() when yaml_data defines a level never observed in the data, and warning() per time-dependent covariate flagging that its REFERENCE still reflects baseline only calls parse_covariate_expression; nested formula_ok, compute_ref_levels, compute_time_dependent; feeds initialize_covariate_search; TIME_DEPENDENT drives covariate placement
validate_param_transformations(covariate_search, data_file, id_col, model_name, models_folder="models") ✓ Fail-fast guard for every population (time-constant) covariate target: parameterization must be classifiable as normal P = TV*EXP(ETA) or log P = EXP(TV+ETA); a log target must have a separate TV_<param> line (inline P = EXP(THETA+ETA) rejected — the additive term would land outside the EXP); rejects disguised-log TV_P = EXP(THETA(n)) and unbalanced parens search table, data, model invisible(TRUE) or stop() with a refactor message readLines; stop() calls detect_param_transform; called-by initialize_covariate_search, prepare_search_base_model

Notes: cov_to_test = beta_<COV>_<PARAM> computed in two places here + in validate_covariate_search_table (dup). Continuous FORMULA vocab is now linear/power/exponential plus user expressions — power1/power0.75 were removed (use power + INIT "1 FIX"/"0.75 FIX"). No schema/action/phase writes here.

R/model-discovery.R

Scans the models folder, parses bbr based_on/notes into DB rows, computes relative step numbers via parent-chain recursion.

Function Exp Purpose Key inputs Returns Side effects Calls / Called-by
discover_existing_models(search_state) ✓ Catalog run\d+.(ctl|mod), read bbr per run, build search_database, assign relative step numbers. Every row it builds is stamped created_by_search = FALSE — it was on disk before the search started, so the search will not submit, retry or status-track it. Status per model comes from get_model_status_from_files(model_path, require_cov_step = search_state$search_config$require_cov_step %||% TRUE), so a search initialized with require_cov_step=FALSE does not mark pre-existing runs failed for lacking a .cov (this works only because initialize_search_config() runs first) search_state (needs $search_config$require_cov_step) updated search_state (+ $discovered_models) cat; list.files; bbr::read_model; stop() (missing base / circular parent) calls initialize_search_database_core, get_model_status_from_files, read_nonmem_ext, get_model_covariates_from_files, dplyr::bind_rows; nested get_step_number, is_descendant_of; called-by initialize_covariate_search

Notes: 4th row-builder — hand-builds the 19-col row (must stay in sync w/ canonical schema), including created_by_search = FALSE. Writes action ∈ {manual_modification(default), retry, add_single_covariate, remove_single_covariate}, phase ∈ {manual(default), retry, individual_testing} — but then overwrites most: phase <- ifelse(retry, phase, "manual"), action <- ifelse(retry, action, "manual_modification"), so only retry survives; base row forced to action="base_model"/phase="base"/step_number=0L. Net: the note-parsing into *_single_covariate is discarded for non-retry models.

R/validation.R

Reads NONMEM output to update DB status/OFV/RSE/ΔOFV; THETA/OMEGA/SIGMA block-format validators; covariate→parameter mapping check.

Function Exp Purpose Key inputs Returns Side effects Calls / Called-by
update_model_status_from_files(search_state, model_name, force=FALSE) ✓ Read .lst/.ext/.cov, set status/ofv/rse_max/issue, compute signed ΔOFV vs parent (only when the model is completed with a non-NA OFV and the parent row exists with an OFV). File resolution is delegated, not hardcoded: the .lst comes from a single read_nonmem_lst(model_path) probe (so the run-dir or control-stream location is found), whose $file locates the listing and whose $status is checked first — a probe of "read_error" returns failed with the probe’s own error_message, never in_progress, because the monitoring loop waits on in_progress and a file that will never become readable would hang it forever. It deliberately does not consume $status == "failed" — see the rejected-designs note in the hazards section. The .ext comes from a single read_nonmem_ext(model_path) call whose result is reused for OFV/parameters, and the .cov is looked for in dirname(lst_file) — wherever the rest of that run’s output actually is. An absent/empty/unparseable .ext now reports read_nonmem_ext()’s own $error message (falling back to "No EXT file found" only when it is empty). The ΔOFV sign is delegated to .signed_delta_ofv(direction=NULL), so this function no longer chooses a convention at all — each row’s own action does, via .is_removal_model(): removal ⇒ child − parent (positive = OFV rose = the removal hurt ⇒ keep the covariate), anything else ⇒ parent − child. NULL is mandatory here: this is a back-fill over a mixed set of rows, so stamping one direction across it would mislabel the other kind. The helper also corrects a retry of a removal — its own action is "retry", which used to fall to the forward branch and record the wrong sign state, name, force; $search_config$require_cov_step (%||% TRUE) updated search_state cat; reads the listing via .read_listing_lines (latin1/skipNul, not bare readLines — only the bbi OUTPUT file is read with readLines); self-heals missing DB cols (13-col required_cols — note action is not in it, which .is_removal_model tolerates by returning FALSE); each missing column is filled with a scalar default of its own type via if/else — the previous dplyr::case_when() there always threw, since its branches mixed NA_real_/FALSE/NA_character_ and case_when requires one shared type, so this recovery path crashed instead of recovering nested read_all_model_files; calls read_nonmem_lst, .read_listing_lines, read_nonmem_ext, extract_nonmem_timestamps, get_param2, .signed_delta_ofv, .resolve_rse_threshold (the high-RSE warning is issued against the limit the search will actually judge the model by, so monitoring output and the selection decision cannot disagree); called-by force_update_models, update_all_model_statuses

Notes: Self-heal schema #2 — update_model_status_from_files declares a 13-col required_cols subset, adds missing via case_when defaults (NA_real_ for numerics, FALSE for excluded_from_step, else NA_character_). Status values it writes: completed/failed/in_progress only — its results$status <- "unknown" initial value and the internal "stopped"/"read_error" LST classifications never reach the DB (every return path overwrites them; read_error — from either the read_nonmem_lst probe or the re-read — becomes failed, matching get_model_status_from_files, and specifically not in_progress). ΔOFV sign: removal (per .is_removal_model) uses child - parent; everything else parent - child (positive=improvement both). Completion needs valid OFV AND (if require_cov_step) a .cov in the directory the .lst was found in; boundary params (abs >= 8.99990e5) → failed. This is deliberately the same test as get_model_status_from_files() — the two readers must agree, or a model changes verdict depending on which one looked.

File I/O & model modification

R/file-io.R

NONMEM file I/O: locate/read/write control files; parse .ext/.lst for status, OFV, covariates, timestamps.

Function Exp Purpose Key inputs Returns Side effects Calls / Called-by
read_model_file(search_state, run_name, extensions=c(".ctl",".mod")) ✓ Read control file, stash path models_folder+run_name char lines w/ file_path attr stop() if none called-by model_add_cov, remove_covariate_from_model
find_model_file(base_path, extensions=c(".ctl",".mod")) ✓ Resolve actual model file path base_path (no ext) full path or NULL — called-by adjust_theta_for_covariate, validation, sim
.read_listing_lines(path) · The one way to read a .lst — plain readLines() is not safe on NONMEM listings. Two-attempt read: the session’s own encoding first, so a valid UTF-8 listing keeps its non-ASCII characters in the text callers quote verbatim (error_excerpt, the #TERM block); on error, a latin1 retry, where every byte maps to a character and nothing can throw (a run that emitted PRDERR output carries stray control bytes, which make readLines() throw “invalid multibyte string” under a UTF-8 locale). skipNul=TRUE on both, so embedded nuls are skipped instead of truncating the file. Status markers are ASCII and stay greppable either way full path to an existing listing character() of lines (warn=FALSE) opens a connection per attempt, closed via on.exit; errors propagate — a path that cannot be opened at all fails both attempts and signals, so every caller wraps it in tryCatch called-by read_nonmem_lst, extract_nonmem_timestamps, update_model_status_from_files (nested read_all_model_files)
write_model_file(search_state, lines) ✓ Write lines back to file_path attr lines w/ attr search_state writeLines; stop() if attr missing called-by model_add_cov, remove_covariate_from_model
read_nonmem_ext(model_path) ✓ OFV+params from .ext (last -1e9 final-estimates line). Fallback: with no -1e9 line it warning()s and parses the last iteration line instead — so a still-estimating run returns a usable-looking OFV, which is why status readers must confirm the run finished first dir or .ext (3 candidates: <path>/<name>.ext, dirname(<path>)/<name>.ext, <path>.ext) list(found, file, ofv, parameters, n_parameters) / list(found=FALSE, error, ofv=NA, parameters=NULL) — distinguishes not-found, “No data lines”, and read error via $error warning() called-by get_model_status_from_files, validation, discovery, scm-algorithm, init
read_nonmem_lst(model_path) ✓ Classify .lst run status via regex (hard-failure markers beat success markers — a plain any() test, not order-aware; then Stop Time: + runtime-error/severe-warning markers, else incomplete). Its $status is a listing verdict, not the search’s success test: no caller treats "failed" here as disqualifying, because success is a usable OFV plus a .cov (see the rejected-designs note in the hazards section); also the resolver for where the output lives — 3 candidates (<path>/<name>.lst, dirname(<path>)/<name>.lst, <path>.lst), so callers use $file/dirname($file) to find sibling output instead of assuming a layout. Reads through .read_listing_lines(), so a listing with non-UTF-8 bytes still classifies dir or .lst list(found, file, status, error_message, error_excerpt, has_issues); status ∈ not_run/incomplete/completed/failed/read_error/invalid_input/invalid_path. $file is present on every path where a listing was resolved — including the read-error handler, which returns found=TRUE, status="read_error" and the path. Dropping $file there used to make an unreadable listing indistinguishable from one NONMEM has not written yet, so callers testing only $file read it as “still running”. The three found=FALSE returns (invalid_input, invalid_path, not_run) carry no $file — calls .read_listing_lines; called-by get_model_status_from_files, update_model_status_from_files, extract_nonmem_timestamps, validate_base_model_for_search
get_model_status_from_files(model_path, require_cov_step=TRUE) ✓ Combine LST+EXT into one status — the file-side definition of “did this run succeed”, matching update_model_status_from_files() so both readers agree. Order matters: finished is established before any OFV is trusted, because read_nonmem_ext() falls back to the last iteration line, so a still-estimating model reports a usable-looking OFV. How minimisation ended is deliberately not part of the test — a run that stopped on rounding errors but produced an OFV and a .cov is a success model path — a run dir or a control-stream base (either reader resolves both), or the .lst itself: a trailing .lst is stripped before either reader runs, because read_nonmem_lst() accepts the listing but read_nonmem_ext() would then hunt for <model>.lst.ext, find nothing, and make a finished run read as failed. Plus require_cov_step char status: "not_run" (neither .lst nor .ext found) · "incomplete" (no .lst, or the .lst’s own status is "incomplete" — which includes an empty listing) · "failed" (the listing resolved but could not be read (read_error) — tested before the OFV, so an unreadable run can never fall through to success; or the .cov is missing under require_cov_step; or the .lst reports completion while the OFV is unusable — a missing/unparseable .ext, which update_model_status_from_files() also reports as failed) · "completed" (OFV non-NA, finite, abs <= 1e10; no parameter at abs >= 8.9999e5; and — when require_cov_step — the .cov exists, its name and directory both taken from the resolved listing (dirname(lst_info$file) + basename(lst_info$file) minus .lst), never from basename(model_path), which would look for <model>.lst.cov) · otherwise the .lst’s own status. No longer returns completed_with_issues — that value is gone from the package. A "completed" verdict therefore always means both halves of the test were met; the .lst alone can never produce one — calls read_nonmem_lst, read_nonmem_ext; called-by validate_base_model_for_search, discover_existing_models
get_model_covariates_from_files(search_state, model_name) ✓ Covariate tag names present via bbr tags $tags (beta_*) char vec (names) or character(0) bbr::read_model called-by discover_existing_models
extract_nonmem_timestamps(model_name, models_folder="models") ✓ Parse start/stop from .lst. Locates the file via read_nonmem_lst(...)$file (run-dir or beside the control stream — no assumed models/<run>/<run>.lst) and reads it with .read_listing_lines(). Parses under LC_TIME="C": the %a/%b in every candidate format are interpreted in the reader’s locale, so on a non-English session none of the layouts matched and both timestamps came back NA with nothing signalled; the original locale is restored via on.exit. The stop marker is matched unanchored with grep("Stop Time:", fixed = TRUE), the same way update_model_status_from_files() tests it, so a leading space cannot make one function call the run finished and the other not name, folder list(start_time, stop_time, found_start, found_stop); on failure list(start_time=NA, stop_time=NA, error=<"LST file not found"/"Empty LST file"/read error>) (no found_* fields on the error paths — callers must not assume them) temporarily switches the session’s LC_TIME to "C" for the duration of the call (on.exit restore, both suppressWarnings) calls read_nonmem_lst, .read_listing_lines; nested parse_nonmem_time; called-by submit_and_wait_for_step, update_model_status_from_files
parse_nonmem_time(line) · nested Parse one NONMEM timestamp line across host locales: builds two candidate strings (zone stripped mid-string " [A-Z]{3,4} ", zone stripped at end "\\s+[A-Z]{3,4}\\s*$") and tries four formats against each — %a %b %d %H:%M:%S %Y, %a %d %b %Y %I:%M:%S %p, %a %d %b %Y %H:%M:%S, %a %b %d %I:%M:%S %p %Y. Each result is tested because as.POSIXct() returns NA on a format mismatch instead of signalling, so tryCatch would never fire. Correctness depends on the caller’s LC_TIME="C" window — the day/month abbreviations NONMEM writes are English one trimmed line POSIXct (first format that parses) or NA (also for non-scalar/NA/empty input) suppressWarnings only nested in extract_nonmem_timestamps; used for both the first line (start) and the line after Stop Time:

Notes: read_nonmem_ext’s $parameters is read now — both get_model_status_from_files and update_model_status_from_files scan it for NONMEM’s boundary marker (abs >= 8.9999e5) before calling a run completed; $n_parameters is still read by no caller. read_nonmem_lst’s $file is likewise load-bearing: it is the single resolver for run-dir-vs-beside-the-.ctl output, and get_model_status_from_files, update_model_status_from_files and extract_nonmem_timestamps all anchor sibling files (.cov) and re-reads to dirname() of it rather than assuming a layout. $file is absent only from the three found=FALSE returns (invalid_input, invalid_path, not_run) — a listing that exists but cannot be read comes back found=TRUE, status="read_error" with $file, which is what lets a caller distinguish “unreadable” from “not written yet”. Test $status, not just $file. Every read of a listing goes through .read_listing_lines() (latin1 + skipNul) — using readLines() directly on a .lst is the bug it exists to prevent. read_model_file’s file_path attr is a hard contract for write_model_file.

R/covariate-formula.R

Registry + source of truth for how a covariate effect is written into NONMEM: one entry per (STATUS, FORMULA), parameter-transform detection, and user expression parsing. Consumed by the WRITE side (model_add_cov) and calculate_covariate_df. The forest READ side (apply_covariate_model) evaluates the model’s own $PK and does not use this registry.

Function Exp Purpose Key inputs Returns Side effects Calls / Called-by
register_covariate_formula(status, formula, nonmem=NULL, init="0.1", categorical=FALSE, nonmem_log=NULL) · Store a form keyed "status.formula". nonmem(cova, ref, n) renders the MULTIPLICATIVE factor for a normal-scale TV; nonmem_log(cova, ref, n) the ADDITIVE term for a log-scale TV; categorical=TRUE flags per-level IF/ELSEIF handling. Internal since 2026-07-28 (@keywords internal/@noRd) — its only caller is this file, 5× at load time to declare the built-ins status, formula, renderer fns invisible(key) assign into the load-time registry env called at load time for the built-ins
get_covariate_formula(status, formula) · Look up an entry; falls through to parse_covariate_expression(formula) when the name isn’t registered, so a raw expression works like a built-in status, formula entry list or NULL — called-by model_add_cov, calculate_covariate_df
list_covariate_formulas() · The registered "status.formula" keys. Internal since 2026-07-28 — sorted character — called-by model_add_cov (the “unknown formula” error message)
detect_param_transform(modelcode, param) · Classify a parameter: "normal" (P = TV*EXP(ETA)), "log" (P = EXP(TV+ETA)), "unknown" (ETA not inside an EXP → exotic, callers reject). No IIV on the parameter ⇒ "normal". Robust to models that already carry covariates model lines, param name character(1) — calls .exp_inner_containing_eta; called-by model_add_cov, validate_param_transformations
.exp_inner_containing_eta(rhs) · Body of the first paren-balanced EXP(...) whose content holds an ETA( (\b guard so THETA( doesn’t match); NA if the ETA isn’t wrapped in an EXP RHS of the parameter line character(1) or NA — called-by detect_param_transform
parse_covariate_expression(formula) · Treat a non-built-in FORMULA as a single-factor expression in reserved cov (and optional ref); every other symbol is an estimated THETA, in order of appearance. Rejects anything using a function outside .COV_EXPR_ALLOWED (+ - * / ^ exp log log10 sqrt) — notably if/ifelse, which keeps expressions single-factor formula string entry list(expr, theta_names, nonmem, nonmem_log, ...) or NULL. nonmem_log is the same rendering joined with + instead of * — the expression is never transformed — all.vars/all.names; called-by get_covariate_formula
.translate_expr_to_nonmem(expr, cova, ref, thetas, n) · AST walk rendering the R expression as NONMEM: cov→covariate column, ref→its value, parameter symbols→THETA(n), THETA(n+1)…, math fns uppercased, ^→** parsed expr character(1) — called-by the expression entry’s nonmem()
parse_named_init(init_str, theta_names) · Split a ;-delimited named INIT spec ("EMAX=0.1; EC50=(0,10,1000)") into one $THETA init string per theta, aligned to theta_names, defaulting to "0.1"; order-independent, unknown names ignored INIT cell, theta names character(length(theta_names)) — called-by model_add_cov (multi-theta path)
.cov_pow_nonmem(cova, ref, n) · Multiplicative power renderer: * (COV/ref)**THETA(n) cova, ref, n character(1) — registered for both con.power and cat.power
.cov_pow_logadd(cova, ref, n) · Additive (log-scale) power renderer: + THETA(n)*LOG(COV/ref) cova, ref, n character(1) — registered for both con.power and cat.power

Registered built-ins (byte-exact mirror of the legacy output):

key normal (* factor) log (+ term)
con.power * (COV/ref)**THETA(n) + THETA(n)*LOG(COV/ref)
con.linear * (1 + (COV-ref) * THETA(n)) + LOG(1 + (COV-ref) * THETA(n))
con.exponential * EXP(THETA(n) * (COV-ref)) + THETA(n) * (COV-ref)
cat.power same as con.power — a numeric-levelled covariate (e.g. dose 35/70/125/150) as a power relation; not categorical, so no IF block same
cat.linear — — (flagged categorical=TRUE; the per-level $PK IF/ELSEIF block stays in model_add_cov)

Notes: power1/power0.75 were removed — express them as power + INIT "1 FIX" / "0.75 FIX". A user expression now carries a nonmem_log too (2026-07-28): the same string joined with + instead of *. So on a log-scale population parameter the expression is ADDED, not multiplied, and it is inserted verbatim — writing it on the log scale (e.g. log(EMAX*cov/(EC50+cov))) is the user’s responsibility, flagged by a WARNING. The package deliberately does NOT wrap it in LOG() for you. The registry’s old read-side r_eval fields are gone — apply_covariate_model evaluates the $PK equations instead, so write and read cannot drift.

Notes: 3rd row-builder — create_retry_model uses template db[1,] + blank + rbind (order-sensitive, not bind_rows): action="retry", phase="retry", retry_attempt=1L, original_model=original, estimation_issue=issue_type, created_by_search=TRUE. Because the rbind is width-sensitive it calls .ensure_provenance_column(search_state) before taking the template. Sets bbr based_on to the original parent (skip failed).

THETA perturbation rules (2026-07-28) — the init comes verbatim from the covariate table’s INIT column, so it can be bounded or FIX. Parsed from the text before the first ; (so a FIX in a comment can’t trigger it):

init form new init note
0.1 -0.1 sign flip, the long-standing rule
(0, 0.1, 3) (0, 1.55, 3) midpoint of the wider side; always strictly inside the bounds
(0, 0.1) (0, 0.05) one-sided: flip if still legal, else midpoint of the bounded side
0.75 FIX untouched a fixed value is a modelling choice, not a starting point

Zero perturbable lines: reason="all_thetas_fixed" (≥1 matched line, all FIX) ⇒ create_retry_model skips the retry entirely; reason="no_theta_lines" (nothing matched) still creates the retry — an identical rerun is legitimate recovery for a Metworx cluster drop. process_estimation_issues maps the skip to action="retry_skipped" (not a failure) and writes SKIPPED_retry_<model>_log.txt. Multi-theta/categorical: FIX and non-FIX thetas of the same covariate are handled per-line, so a partly-FIX covariate still retries.

R/scm-evaluation.R

The one acceptance test (.evaluate_model_criteria) every phase and caller judges a model by, plus the “pick a model” helpers built on it.

Function Exp Purpose Key inputs Returns Side effects Calls / Called-by
.evaluate_model_criteria(search_state, model_names, phase=c("forward", "backward"), p_value=NULL, rse_threshold=NULL) · THE single answer to “may the search use this model” — status completed AND ΔOFV clearing the χ² threshold for that covariate’s own df AND the RSE test, which is now require_cov_step-dependent: default TRUE rejects an unreadable rse_max, FALSE accepts it (see Notes). phase is not just a different p-value: forward and backward store delta_ofv with opposite sign conventions (fwd parent − model, positive = better; bwd model − base, positive = worse) and compare it in opposite directions (> vs <), so the phase selects both. RSE test is identical in both, but what passing it authorises differs (fwd accepts the covariate, bwd accepts its removal). Reads the DB only — the caller must have written delta_ofv to the row first model_names, phase, p-value (defaults to the phase’s config), rse data.frame, one row per name found in the DB, in the order given: model_name, status, ofv, delta_ofv, rse_max, covariate_df, ofv_threshold, meets_ofv, meets_rse, meets_threshold, note; the same 11-col frame with 0 rows when the DB is empty/no name matches. The column names are the ones evaluate_removal_impacts() reports, so its result frame is assembled straight from these none — pure read, no cat/stop/write. A missing DB column reads as all-NA rather than erroring (a checkpoint predating rse_max still evaluates — on OFV alone only when require_cov_step=FALSE; under the default it now fails the RSE test); tag/df lookup errors are swallowed to df=1. meets_ofv/meets_rse/meets_threshold are NA-coerced to FALSE before returning: they are the contract every consumer indexes on, and x[NA] in R returns NA rather than dropping the element, so one NA verdict became an NA model name out of get_significant_models_from_step — a model that does not exist. Fails closed calls .resolve_rse_threshold, extract_covariate_name_from_tag, calculate_covariate_df, pvalue_to_threshold; called-by select_best_model, .best_acceptable_model, get_significant_models_from_step, evaluate_removal_impacts, nested get_selection_info (scm-results.R)
.best_acceptable_model(search_state, model_names, p_value=NULL, rse_threshold=NULL) · Lowest-OFV model among those meeting the criteria. Backs every “which model do we carry forward” decision that is not a single step’s winner — the redemption re-base, the post-redemption overall pick, and the fallbacks either side. Those sites used to take which.min(ofv) over completed models with no acceptance test at all, which is how a model failing the RSE limit could become the base for backward elimination purely on fit. Judges with phase="forward" (hardwired). Contract: the base model is never returned — it carries no delta_ofv, so it cannot pass meets_ofv. It is the incumbent, not a candidate; a caller needing a fallback when nothing qualifies must name one itself candidate model_names, p-value, rse list(model, rejected) — model is NULL when nothing qualifies; rejected = status %in% "completed" & meets_ofv & !meets_rse & !is.na(ofv), i.e. only completed models that had the fit to win and lost on RSE, so a model excluded for some other reason is not announced as an RSE rejection none calls .evaluate_model_criteria; called-by run_scm_selective_forward (×4: fallback base, redemption-base fallback, per-redemption-step re-base, overall best)
.report_rse_rejections(rejected, context) · Name the models that had the fit to win but failed the RSE limit, so an RSE-driven choice is legible in the log at the time it is made instead of only in a later report the rejected element of .best_acceptable_model(), a context string invisible(NULL) cat (one ⚠️ line per rejected model) called-by run_scm_selective_forward (×4, paired with each .best_acceptable_model call)
select_best_model(search_state, model_names, p_value=NULL, rse_threshold=NULL) ✓ Pick the highest-ΔOFV model clearing its df-specific χ² threshold + RSE. Re-reads outputs, back-fills delta_ofv from the parent where missing — through .signed_delta_ofv(direction="forward"), stated rather than derived because this function also fixes the test’s direction (phase="forward" below); deriving would store a removal as model − parent and then test that same row with delta_ofv > threshold, so a removal costing 70 OFV points would read as a 70-point improvement and be selected. warning()s when handed a removal model, since that means the caller assembled model_names wrongly — then delegates the verdict to .evaluate_model_criteria(phase="forward") and copies its columns onto the local frame as covariate_df/ofv_threshold/delta_ofv_significant/rse_acceptable/overall_significant/evaluation_notes model_names, p-value, rse list(search_state, best_model, significant_models, evaluation_results, criteria_used, status); status="no_completed_models" short-circuit when nothing completed mutates delta_ofv in both the local frame and search_state$search_database for rows missing it (this is what the evaluator then reads back); cat calls update_all_model_statuses, .resolve_rse_threshold, .signed_delta_ofv, .evaluate_model_criteria, pvalue_to_threshold (display line only); called-by forward drivers + orchestrator

Notes: Threshold per-model from covariate df (default df=1 when unresolved). The “NA RSE is acceptable everywhere” rule is retired (2026-08-07) — it held for the whole earlier life of this file, so discard any memory of it. meets_rse now follows search_config$require_cov_step (%||% TRUE), and the test is identical(require_cov, FALSE), not isTRUE(require_cov) — only an explicit FALSE relaxes the rule; NA, "yes", a vector, or a missing search_config are all strict. The isTRUE form failed open: every malformed value fell through to the lenient branch and silently switched the RSE criterion off, which is the opposite of .resolve_rse_threshold’s treatment of a bad threshold. initialize_search_config() stores whatever it is handed, so the guard has to live here. So: default/strict ⇒ !is.na(rse_max) & rse_max < limit, an unreadable RSE REJECTS the model; explicit FALSE ⇒ the old is.na(rse_max) | rse_max < limit. The two settings are one question asked twice — a search that demands a covariance step cannot accept a model whose precision it could not read, and one that does not demand it must not reject a model for lacking something it never asked for. An unknown RSE prints as "NA", never 0%, and its note reads “RSE unavailable (a successful covariance step is required)” rather than NA% > 50%, which would hide which of the two failures happened. select_best_model’s best = which.max(delta_ofv) among significant rows (fit-ranked), while .best_acceptable_model’s best = which.min(ofv) among acceptable rows — different orderings on purpose: one ranks a step’s candidates against a shared parent, the other ranks models from different steps against each other. Re-reads outputs via update_all_model_statuses first.

run_scm_selective_forward(search_state, base_model_id=NULL, forward_p_value=NULL, rse_threshold=NULL, auto_submit=TRUE, auto_retry=TRUE, resume=FALSE) ✓ Selective forward: first step = all covariates; later steps = only covariates from prior significant models; then redemption. resume=TRUE (from continue_search) makes the FIRST pass a continuation (selective from get_step_models(last_step)) instead of “test all”. Every continuation pass first blocks until the previous step is terminal: a repeat loop takes the previous step’s non-base rows, and while any is pending per .is_pending_status() it prints them, Sys.sleep(60)s and re-runs update_all_model_statuses(). Needed because get_step_models() reads only status=="completed" rows, so a model still running on the cluster would be invisible and the loop would create the next step (or a redemption model) on top of it. Every re-base goes through .best_acceptable_model() (4 sites: fallback base when a step has no winner, the redemption-base fallback, the per-redemption-step re-base, and the final post-redemption pick) — each used to rank on OFV alone, so a model the search itself had rejected could become the base everything after it builds on, including the model handed to backward elimination. Each site pairs with .report_rse_rejections(), and the final pick prints when it overrides the step winner. No site treats “nothing qualifies” as terminal — since .best_acceptable_model() never returns the base model, each names its own fallback: the fallback base pick uses prev_step$base_model (else base_model_id), the redemption-base fallback uses base_model_id, the per-redemption-step re-base keeps the current_redemption_base it already had, and the overall pick keeps the step winner. All four pools exclude backward rows via !.scm_backward_rows(search_state) — all_previous_models (fallback base pick), all_main_models (redemption-base fallback), all_models_so_far (per-redemption-step re-base), all_completed_candidates (overall pick) — because a backward row’s delta_ofv carries the opposite sign convention and the forward test would read a costly removal as a large improvement. Enforced by the test “every forward candidate pool in the file carries the phase filter”, which greps the source for the four pool assignments and fails if any lacks the filter, so a fifth pool or a deleted guard breaks loudly. The filter deliberately keeps the base model in all_main_models: the base row’s phase is "base", which .scm_phase_is_backward does not match, so it stays in scope — load-bearing, because that site falls back to base_model_id when nothing qualifies and then looks it up in this very table (final_best_idx <- which(all_main_models$model_name == final_best_model)); filtering it out would leave integer(0) and make GUARD 2 skip redemption base, p-value, rse, resume list(search_state, status, final_best_model, step_results, total_time_minutes) save_search_state() at 5 points, all named by .scm_checkpoint_name() → <models_folder>/scm_rds/NN_forward_created.rds, NN_forward_done.rds, NN_redemption_created.rds, NN_redemption_done.rds, NN_forward_complete.rds; Sys.sleep(60) polling in the continuation guard; cat calls get_remaining_covariates, .is_pending_status, update_all_model_statuses, get_step_models, get_significant_models_from_step, get_covariates_from_models, get_model_covariates_from_db, run_univariate_step, submit_and_wait_for_step, select_best_model, .best_acceptable_model, .report_rse_rejections, .resolve_rse_threshold, pvalue_to_threshold, .scm_checkpoint_name, save_search_state; called-by orchestrator + continue_search

Notes: run_scm_selective_forward = the biggest fn (main loop + Scenario A/B redemption). Fresh vs. continuation is an explicit resume flag (init is_continuation <- isTRUE(resume), then TRUE after the first pass) — not inferred from the DB, because the base model can sit at any step_number (it’s tagged phase=="base", not fixed at step 0). The continuation branch reconstructs the previous step from the DB via get_step_models, so no in-memory step_results is needed to resume. resume_selective_forward was removed earlier (forward-only, broken); continue_search (below) replaces it for both phases.

.scm_backward_rows(search_state) · “Which rows carry a backward-signed delta_ofv” — the filter that keeps backward rows out of forward selection’s candidate pools. The two phases store delta_ofv with opposite sign conventions, so a removal that badly worsened the fit reads to the forward test as a large improvement; a search that begins with backward elimination has exactly such rows. A row counts as backward if EITHER its phase says so OR its action does (by_phase | .is_removal_model(search_state, db$model_name)) — neither alone suffices. phase is overwritten by two paths (create_retry_model() writes "retry"; discover_existing_models() rewrites rebuilt rows to "manual"), so phase-only missed a retry of a failed removal — which is not hypothetical, since a retry inherits the original’s step_number and its delta_ofv starts NA but is overwritten with the backward sign the moment the model completes. action closes it because .is_removal_model() resolves a retry to the model it retries — the same resolution update_model_status_from_files() uses to choose the sign in the first place, which is what makes the match exactly as retry-aware as the code that created the sign, rather than merely broader. The base model is matched by neither test (phase="base", action="base_model") so it stays in scope, which the redemption-base fallback depends on search_state (not a bare db — .is_removal_model needs the state) logical vector, one element per database row; logical(0) for NULL / non-data.frame DB. Degrades safely: no phase column ⇒ phase term all-FALSE; no action column ⇒ .is_removal_model all-FALSE; the union is whichever evidence survives none calls .scm_phase_is_backward, .is_removal_model; called-by run_scm_selective_forward (all four of its candidate pools — see that row)

Notes: No new state field — scm_type/full_scm are args (DB doesn’t record the forward method; thresholds come from search_config). Method/phase re-entry reuses the existing methods: standard fwd and backward are already DB-driven (pass the current best as the start); selective fwd gets resume=TRUE. Forward is skipped (jump to backward) when the last step yielded no significant model. Requires the last step to be fully terminal — the test is .is_pending_status() (created/submitted/in_progress/incomplete/unknown), not an inline vector, so the "incomplete" spelling that get_model_status_from_files/discovery write is caught too; else it returns incomplete_step with the offending model names. Winner + significance for the last forward step come from get_step_models (same evaluator as the live selective loop; RSE-aware) — the old .scm_current_best_forward heuristic was removed.

Why the backward-row filter tests two fields (closed 2026-08-07): .scm_backward_rows used to key on phase alone, and a retry launders it — create_retry_model writes phase="retry" while keeping the original’s step_number, and the delta is later filled with the backward sign because .is_removal_model() resolves the retry back to the removal it retries. The row was backward in substance, "retry" in phase, and carried a non-NA backward-signed delta straight into all four forward pools. The fix ORs in .is_removal_model(), the same predicate the sign-writer consults — so the filter and the sign cannot disagree by construction.

Sign/direction consistency — the current, settled picture (2026-08-07). Three mechanisms interlock, and all three now read the same predicate: 1. .signed_delta_ofv() is the sole writer of the ΔOFV sign; .is_removal_model() is the sole direction lookup; .scm_backward_rows() is the sole pool filter, ORing phase with that same lookup. 2. .is_removal_model() itself now falls back to phase for rows whose action cannot answer, so the older failure — a database with no action column giving a removal the forward sign while .scm_backward_rows read it as backward from its phase — is gone. The two readers can no longer disagree on such a row. action remains authoritative where present; a phase that contradicts it is left as a fault to report. 3. The residual risk is no longer a silent disagreement but a mis-assembled candidate list, and both direction-stating callers (select_best_model, evaluate_removal_impacts) warning() on being handed a model of the wrong kind. That is the one seam left, and it is loud.

.signed_delta_ofv(search_state, model_name, model_ofv, reference_ofv, direction=NULL) · The one place the ΔOFV sign convention is chosen. An ADDITION stores reference − model (positive = the covariate improved the fit); a REMOVAL stores model − reference (positive = dropping it made the fit worse). With direction=NULL it is read from the row via .is_removal_model() — the same predicate the acceptance tests and .scm_backward_rows use, which is what stops a row’s stored delta and the rule that later reads it from disagreeing. See the direction rule below the table before choosing state, model name, its OFV, the reference OFV (parent for forward, step base for backward), optional direction numeric(1); NA_real_ if either OFV is missing or zero-length none calls .is_removal_model; called-by update_model_status_from_files (NULL — writes only), select_best_model ("forward") and evaluate_removal_impacts ("backward"), both of which also fix the test’s direction and warn on the other kind
decode_dataset(data, yaml_file, column_names) ✓ Replace numeric category codes with their decoded labels for the named columns, using a spec/lookup’s values→decode mapping data, lookup/spec, columns data with decoded columns — used by the plotting/EDA side

Notes: analyze_* contain duplicate run1→BASE / \d{3}$→RETRY regex; both are exported-but-unused. tags_list arg unused. No globalVariables/@importFrom here.

.DEFAULT_RSE_THRESHOLD (= 50) is a package-level constant, not a function, so it has no row above. It is the one place the default RSE limit lives: initialize_search_config() writes it into a new search’s config and .resolve_rse_threshold() falls back to it, so the value a search is created with and the value an older state is read with cannot drift apart.

When to pass .signed_delta_ofv(direction=) and when not to — the rule, not just the signature. direction looks like a wart; it is not. action is not in update_model_status_from_files()’s self-heal required_cols, so a database can legitimately lack the column. The rule turns on what the caller ALSO does, not on whether its rows are of one kind: - Writes the sign AND fixes the acceptance test’s direction ⇒ state direction to match, and warn on the other kind. Both evaluate_removal_impacts (phase="backward" ⇒ direction="backward") and select_best_model (phase="forward" is a literal ⇒ direction="forward") are in this case. Deriving instead lets the sign and the test disagree whenever the lookup cannot answer: a removal row stored as model − parent (say +50) and then tested with delta_ofv > threshold reads as a 50-point improvement and gets selected. - Writes only, never tests ⇒ leave direction NULL and let each row’s own action decide. update_model_status_from_files is the sole such caller.

Get this backwards and the failure is silent — a stored delta whose sign disagrees with the rule that reads it. Once sign and test agree, the only way left to be wrong is a mis-assembled candidate list, which is why both direction-stating callers warning() when handed a model of the opposite kind.

Names come from the comment’s 2nd ; field, the log flag from its 4th. Only THETAs are ever rescaled: a ;LOG theta is stored as log(value); OMEGA/SIGMA are variances and are reported as NONMEM wrote them (no CV% conversion — that is a model_report() rendering choice, not a trajectory one) ext_cols = full .ext column names (pre-drop, so per-record counts match the control stream), model name, models dir list(labels=<named chr, one per ext col>, log_cols=<chr, columns to exp()>) warning() only, never stop(): control stream unreadable → everything falls back to .ext names/values; per-record count mismatch → that record alone is skipped (named in the message) while the others are still applied calls extract_model_params (via tryCatch+suppressWarnings) → reads control stream from disk; called-by plot_nonmem_iterations
plot_nonmem_iterations(model_name, models_dir="models", transform=TRUE, skip_iterations=0, obj_var="OBJ", max_iterations=100) ✓ Faceted ggplot of the objective column + non-fixed parameter trajectories for the last non-Evaluation $EST step (the only step, if there is just one); BURN iterations renumbered to precede ITER name, dir; transform=TRUE names panels from the control stream and exponentiates ;LOG THETAs (see .listing_column_meta), FALSE plots the .ext verbatim — raw values and raw column names; obj_var takes the .ext column name (THETA1, not CL — it selects before annotations are read); max_iterations is an ITERATION ceiling, not a count; skip_iterations drops that many from the start of each $EST ggplot stop() on non-scalar model_name, missing .ext, empty/iteration-free data, non-logical transform, or obj_var not a column of the .ext (message lists available columns); inherits .listing_column_meta’s warnings calls read_ext_iterations, .listing_column_meta (passing ext_cols, captured from the full .ext before constant columns are dropped, so per-record counts match the control stream regardless of obj_var and FIX-parameter removal), tidyr::pivot_longer, dplyr::filter, ggplot2::

Notes: Own utils::globalVariables(c("ITERATION","TYPE","value","variable")). Uses @import ggplot2 (full). read_ext_iterations’ data.frame is consumed positionally by sample_individual_thetas (col 2 → OBJ), so its column layout/TYPE labels are a hard contract. plot_nonmem_iterations also depends on that layout, but by name: it takes the parameter columns as everything between col 2 and the OBJ column, so obj_var other than "OBJ" must still sit inside that span. The CV%/;LOG rules are a fourth consumer of the $THETA trans annotation (see the ×3 parser note above) — it reuses extract_model_params rather than reparsing, so keep it that way.

Exposure-forest simulation pipeline (7 files)

Data flow: sample_individual_thetas → create_covariate_table → apply_covariate_model (via build_scenario_parameters) → simulate_scenario_profiles → plot_exposure_forest. create_covariate_boxplots is a separate branch.

R/apply-covariate-model.R

Function Exp Purpose Key inputs Returns Side effects Calls / Called-by
apply_covariate_model(model_name, covariate_search, individual_thetas, covariates, models_folder="models") ✓(in NAMESPACE) Evaluate the model’s $PK equations (ETA=0, THETA from draws, covariates from scenario/REFERENCE) → natural-scale structural params for one scenario. Handles log/normal/categorical/multi-theta uniformly (equation’s EXP does the transform once) — no transform detection, no read-side registry, no drift. Small $PK interpreter with IF/ELSEIF/ENDIF + operator translation search table (+REFERENCE), raw estimation-scale thetas, one scenario data.frame(ID, structural THETA cols) natural scale readLines; warning/stop self-contained; called-by build_scenario_parameters
get_block/first_theta_index · nested Control-stream parsing: get_block(tag) returns the lines of every $<tag> record (header + body up to the next $), first_theta_index(txt) returns the first THETA(n) index in an expression — that is how a $PK definition line is pinned to the structural THETA position it defines lines (closed over), block tag / expression text character block lines / integer (NA_integer_ when none) — nested in apply_covariate_model; forest-plots.R’s .structural_param_names carries a duplicate pair
nm_to_r/eval_r/is_active/do_assign · nested The $PK interpreter: translate NONMEM operators (**→^, .EQ., .GE., .AND., .NOT., …) to R, evaluate a fragment in the THETA/ETA/covariate environment, test whether the innermost IF/ELSEIF/ELSE branch is active, and assign LHS = RHS into that environment. This is what makes categorical IF(COV.EQ.x) blocks work with no level→theta table expression text / one $PK line translated string / evaluated value / logical / invisible() writes into the eval env e; skipped <<- accumulates un-evaluable lines for the closing warning() nested in apply_covariate_model

Notes: No longer a reconciliation target — since the read path was rewritten (2026-07-20) it evaluates the model’s own $PK instead of re-deriving the covariate algebra, so the hardcoded factor list (power/linear/exponential, categorical 1 + beta) and the registry r_eval fields are gone. It still parses $THETA order/names and the $PK IF(COV.EQ.x) blocks (level→theta relies on that numeric-level parse — the $THETA name carries the decoded label, not the level). Contract: the downstream mrgsolve model must use the returned THETA columns as natural-scale structural params (no EXP(), no covariate terms) or the effect is double-counted. man/apply_covariate_model.Rd exists.
